clue.text: Kind mother?

definitions.meaning: one's kind is one's basic character or temperament
Mother ... is the personified force behind the natural world

explanation.surface: A short query: is this woman a kindly mother?
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means essential character, and the personified mother of all living things is a familiar figure.

clue.text: When they're busy, they've nothing on

definitions.text: When they're busy, they've nothing on

parts.words: When they're busy, they've nothing on
parts.note: nothing on usually means idle, but here it means wearing no clothes while active

explanation.definitionFit: Naturists go about their activities unclothed.

clue.text: Drink made from brown leaves? Not half!

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: Not half! keeps only one half of the word for leaves

parts.note: goes means leaves

explanation.surface: A beverage brewed from browned leaves? Very much so!
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British fizzy orange soft drink brand. 'Not half!' is British slang for emphatic yes, here meaning keep only half.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy British soft drink brand bears this name, also a Latin dance.

clue.text: Took time out squeezing muscle to be admired

indicators.note: squeezing means holding another word tightly inside

parts.note: rested means took time out
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder took a break from flexing to be admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in high esteem is admired.

clue.text: Exercise books lose one 11s

definitions.note: plural of the answer to 11 across: small rounded rocks

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: lose says a letter drops out of what comes before

parts.note: the Bibles are books of scripture
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Exercise books in a classroom go missing, cross-referenced to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth small rocks found on a beach are a kind of the 11-across answer.

clue.text: Questions about IT? No one notices

indicators.note: about means going round something

parts.note: posers are difficult questions

indicators.note: No tells us to take a letter out of the word before

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Asking about computers, and nobody pays attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No one' removes I from IT, leaving T, which POSERS goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed bills put up on walls are public notices.

clue.text: Not interested in meals being delivered?

indicators.note: being delivered means being spoken, as a speech is delivered

parts.note: board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent to having food brought to the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery suggests takeaway food but means speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking interest and wearied by dullness are the same state.

clue.text: Sparkling wine for meat course, almost cooked

parts.note: lamb is a meat

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared in new order
almost drops the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sparkling wine pairs with the meat dish, which is nearly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes E from COURSE; 'cooked' turns COURS into RUSCO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian red frizzante from Emilia is a sparkling wine.

clue.text: Criticises 11s

definitions.meaning: to slate is to criticise harshly
plural of the 11-across answer: here flat grey roofing rock

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh reviews and grey roofing tiles share this word.

clue.text: Utter problem — there's no time for pieces of 11

indicators.note: Utter is the verb to speak, so the word built here is to be pronounced rather than written

parts.note: trouble is a problem; with no T (time) it leaves rouble, the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A total problem: no time for broken bits of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like 'total' but means speak; ROUBLE (Russian currency) is the word said.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken fragments of masonry and rock are what remain after demolition.

clue.text: Do Russian rebels become old-fashioned types?

indicators.note: the letters rebel against their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political question: do Russian rebels turn into reactionaries?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' reads as a noun but is a verb signalling the anagram of DO RUSSIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, people hopelessly behind the times are called extinct prehistoric reptiles.

clue.text: After drink, sailor twirls to dance

indicators.note: After puts the sailor following the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit drink

indicators.note: twirls means the word for sailor turns round

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor, having had a drink, spins round to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance in quick rhythm is named by the answer.

clue.text: Stoke-on-Trent's code is a gem

parts.note: ST is the postcode area for Stoke-on-Trent
a means one, a single

explanation.surface: A trivia fact about the Potteries town's postcode being precious.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke-on-Trent is an English city in Staffordshire; British postcodes start with letters for the area.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious jewel is often called a precious rock of that kind.

clue.text: Plant on which money might grow?

definitions.text: Plant on which money might grow?

parts.words: Plant on which money might grow?
parts.note: bread is slang for money, so a tree bearing it would grow cash; the breadfruit plant has this name

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash plus a woody plant gives a name for the breadfruit, a tropical fruiting plant.

clue.text: Clever person — Sting, that is

parts.note: to smart is to sting
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A remark that the musician Sting is a brainy sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the singer, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all or smart alec is informally called by this word, also a sweet's brand name.

clue.text: Fighting animal volunteers upset leader

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down

parts.note: a cat is an animal
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: A pugnacious creature unsettles the volunteers' commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the offensive in a battle is being in combat.

clue.text: US fruit drink

definitions.meaning: in America gourds such as courgettes and pumpkins go by this name
a British concentrated fruit cordial diluted with water

explanation.surface: A label: an American fruit beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an American gourd vegetable and the British diluted cordial.

clue.text: Foreign articles close to home in war briefs, perhaps

parts.note: un is French for a and der is German for the

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another
close to means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Foreign items close to home during wartime: legal papers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign articles' are UN (French) and DER (German); E from 'close to home' goes 'in' WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are an example of garments worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Grounds for first divorce? I traded in sober adult

indicators.note: the first letter of divorce is the one the I swaps with
traded means the I changes places within the word

parts.note: staid means sober, serious
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Legal grounds for divorce: one partner trading in a dull grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first divorce' is D; 'I traded' swaps I with that D in STAIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports arenas, using the Latin plural, are grounds for games.

clue.text: Declares at cricket matches

parts.note: Tests are international cricket matches

explanation.surface: Someone makes a statement at the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Test matches are multi-day international cricket fixtures; 'declares' is also a cricket term, adding misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness to something formally is to declare it true.

clue.text: Foundation of plot 11

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden
the 11-across answer means a rock

explanation.surface: The base of a garden plot is laid with stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid rock beneath soil is figuratively the fundamental basis of anything.

clue.text: Quarrel breaking out nearby

indicators.note: breaking out means the letters break their order

explanation.surface: A fight erupts close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A barney is British slang for a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for a noisy argument or row.

clue.text: German philosopher covers the Spanish, English or Finnish instrument

indicators.note: covers in a down clue means sits on top of what follows

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A German thinker discusses Spanish, English or Finnish music.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked zither-like folk harp from Finland bears this name.

clue.text: Enough to get you drunk: no end of drink — is that morally wrong?

indicators.note: no says a letter is taken away

parts.note: a skinful is enough alcohol to make one drunk

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A moral question about drinking a skinful without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of drink' removes K from SKINFUL; 'no end' looks like 'endless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked conduct, breaking religious or moral law, is morally wrong.

clue.text: It can help one get a start in life

definitions.text: It can help one get a start in life

parts.words: It can help one get a start in life
parts.note: a machine that keeps eggs or premature babies warm, or a scheme nurturing new businesses

explanation.definitionFit: Warmed apparatus hatches eggs and supports premature babies, giving them their first days.

clue.text: '40s actress is teetotal and fit, eating yogurt regularly

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside

parts.note: be is the verb that is is a form of
able means fit, capable

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter

explanation.surface: A wartime film star kept healthy with no drink and lots of yogurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes YGR from yogurt; 'eating' puts it inside BETTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous pin-up Hollywood star of the 1940s, known for her legs.

clue.text: Rule, which comes from above, they say

indicators.note: they say signals a word that sounds the same

parts.note: rain falls from the sky above

explanation.surface: Authority that descends from on high, as people put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests divine right; the precipitation is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's rule is a period of sovereign power.

clue.text: Encircle part of Britain or Belgium

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Surround some region of Britain or Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose within a circle or sphere is a poetic word for encircling.

clue.text: 11's fine dressing

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: some rock makes a good bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard grey silica rock used for striking sparks is a type of the 11-across answer.

clue.text: Docker does exert, working shifts 10 to 5

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order
shifts here means one letter is changed into another

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A dock worker labours hard on shifts from ten to five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts 10 to 5' turns the X of DOES EXERT into V, giving DOESEVERT; 'working' rearranges it. The shift hours are the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A dock labourer who loads and unloads ships is called by this word.

clue.text: Spooner to ask for stories as extras

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words

parts.note: to beg is to ask for
lies are stories, untruths

explanation.surface: Spooner asks for tales as additional items.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BEG LIES gives the cricket term. In cricket, these are runs scored off the batter's body, counted as extras rather than to the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs off the pad in cricket go into the extras column rather than the batter's score.
